scenes.text: THERE'S A PAGE I NEVER TURNED
scenes.narration: There is a page in the lost property log I have never turned. It sits between page forty-three and page forty-five, and it has no number.
scenes.imagePrompt: A thick old ledger opened in the middle, one page standing upright between the others, edges yellowed, lit by a desk lamp, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.subtext: Every line is something of mine.
scenes.narration: The entries on it go back thirty years. Every line is something I lost.
scenes.imagePrompt: Close-up of a ledger page of faded handwritten rows in several shades of ink, brown with age, too small to read, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.subtext: I lost it on a trip.
scenes.narration: My school blazer. A bicycle bell. The house key I lost in 1991, the week we moved.
scenes.imagePrompt: A child's dark school blazer folded on a steel shelf beside an old bicycle bell and a single brass house key, each tied to a brown luggage tag, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: The claimed by column is empty all the way down. Nothing on that page has ever been collected. They are all on the shelves behind me.
scenes.imagePrompt: Rows of steel shelves stretching back into darkness inside a wire mesh cage, crowded with old tagged belongings, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain
